svg.title: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead of taking anyone's word for it: Only an explicit local request may replace an image reference
svg.text: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead
of taking anyone's word for it
Scenario: Only an explicit local request may replace an image reference
A developer rewrites the references, a reviewer accepts them

g.text: Given a reference image and a captured page differ visibly in their
pixels
The page under test, as Chromium captures it: the box labelled Current is now orange. The
committed reference image of this page has both boxes in blue, so the two images differ in
their pixels.
A throwaway copy of the toolbox holds that reference twice, once for each of the suite's two
visual checks, and one test that compares the page with both.
Then a flag set to zero, like no flag at all, is not passed on, and both checks refuse the
difference
Each card types the same line with another setting. First, what task project:test:e2e would hand to its test container:
with the flag set to 0, the bare command, so the test never sees the flag.
Then the test itself, run with the 0 anyway. Both checks fail on "Visual mismatch", the run exits with the code 1, and
git status prints nothing: both references are untouched. No flag at all gives the same result.

text.tspan: TASK_E2E_UPDATE_BASELINES=0 task --dry project:test:e2e 2>&1 | grep -o "exec -T.* codeceptjs node";

g.text: And in CI the flag set to 1 reaches the test with CI set, and both checks refuse to rewrite
anything
Same line, as a CI job would run it, with the flag set to 1. The task hands the flag over together with CI=true, so the
test knows where it runs.
Both checks refuse at once, "TASK_E2E_UPDATE_BASELINES is forbidden in CI", and git sees no change. In CI, a visual
difference can only fail the run.

text.tspan: CI=true TASK_E2E_UPDATE_BASELINES=1 task --dry project:test:e2e 2>&1 | grep -o "exec -T.* codeceptjs node";

g.text: When the flag is exactly 1 on the developer's machine, both references are rewritten with
the captured pixels
Same line on the developer's machine, with the flag set to 1. The task hands the flag over, and both checks pass: each
one wrote the captured page over its reference.
git status now lists the two references as modified. Nothing is accepted yet: someone still has to look at them.

text.tspan: TASK_E2E_UPDATE_BASELINES=1 task --dry project:test:e2e 2>&1 | grep -o "exec -T.* codeceptjs node";

g.text: Then the merge request shows each old reference next to its new pixels, for a reviewer to
accept
The developer commits the two references on a branch and opens a merge request, a change a reviewer accepts or refuses.
For each image, GitLab shows the old reference, all blue, next to the new capture with its orange box.
That is the only road for a new reference: rewritten on a developer's machine, then looked at by a person before it
reaches the main branch.

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 5 steps · 5 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
● Given: stage ● When: actions ● Then: proofs
